text: Huh, I'm rinsing with just water, but the oil's still there. Why won't it go?
Water and oil are just opposites by nature, so plain water alone can never mix with it.
But soap molecules are what's called surfactants - one end loves water, the other end loves oil.
So it wraps around the grease droplet, forming a tiny ball called a micelle. That micelle floats in the water, so it rinses away with everything else.
That's also why you're supposed to scrub your hands for at least 20 seconds - it takes soap that long to wrap around germs and lift them off your skin.
Viruses like coronavirus have a fatty outer layer, so soap can literally burst that layer and disable them.
By the way, soap has been around for a very long time. The earliest versions were just fat mixed with ash.
